features.feature: Unknown content-stream operators outside and inside BX/EX
features.requirement: §7.8.2 ordinarily says an unknown operator causes an error. Balanced, nestable BX/EX compatibility sections cause unknown operators and their operands to be ignored without error. BX/EX are not graphics objects or graphics state.
features.assessment: Direct assertion bodies distinguish unknown operator outside (reported), inside (suppressed), after the close (reported again), and nested sections (inner close does not end outer silence). The implementation depth-counts sections and clears unknown operands. Existing tests assert reports but do not assert that valid surrounding artwork is unchanged; a standalone public-raster draft supplies that independent visible control. Existing stray test actually has a balanced BX/EX followed by an unknown operator; it does not test unmatched EX or an unclosed BX. Those are invalid producer input because the pair shall occur; the source does not prescribe recovery, so current saturating/no-report behavior is recorded as policy rather than a conformance defect.

features.requirement: Catalog /Extensions is a direct dictionary. Prefix entries must be registered developer-prefix names and values are direct developer-extension dictionaries, or PDF 2.0 arrays of them. Table 49 fields and direct-object constraints are producer rules. BaseVersion and ExtensionLevel are required; URL is required by EC3 #732; ExtensionRevision is optional. #239 changes the ExtensionLevel monotonic-over-time wording from shall to should.
features.errata: Primary page images primary-0157.png and primary-0158.png show #732 replacing Table 49 URL's old Optional wording with Required, #399 amending the BaseVersion comparison sentence, and #239 demoting the over-time ExtensionLevel sequence to should. `doc/errata-read.md` records the same issue locators. `doc/md/` remains base-text transcription and retains the pre-#732 optional text.
features.assessment: The first test reads two prefixes and the PDF 2.0 extension array form; its second ISO item omits the now-required URL yet is still parsed and retained, which is a reader-tolerance choice rather than producer conformance. It tests the positive URL field on the first entry and demonstrates reading an extension without URL. The negative test only covers missing ExtensionLevel; no assertion isolates missing BaseVersion. The code parses BaseVersion and level but does not enforce BaseVersion <= document version; it retains URL as Option and ExtensionRevision as optional text. Those omitted validity checks are producer constraints; no reader rejection obligation was found. `Extensions::read` is public but had no production caller in the searched workspace; it is not a user-facing compatibility warning path by itself.

features.feature: Annex E name classes and unknown extension data
features.requirement: Annex E.1 requires developers to conform when adding extension data and delegates processors that lack a developer-specific feature to Annex I. E.2 defines first-class, registered-prefix second-class, and private `XX` third-class names. #229 refines the second-class exception to ‘except where otherwise stated in this specification’; #340 changes third-class registration from not necessary to explicitly prohibited. Annex I.3 says unknown dictionary entries behave as absent; unknown features are handled feature by feature. These rules do not require a reader to reject unfamiliar key names or validate a producer's registered prefix.
features.errata: No direct E.1 change found. On physical p.893 / printed p.878, #229 amends the second-class exception; #340 makes private third-class names unregistrable while retaining the `XX` prefix.
features.assessment: The E audit inventory is already parent-reviewed for conditional writer scope: no production writer emits developer extensions or private `XX` names, so no current producer output can certify those Annex E obligations. Reader tests demonstrate the Annex I distinction for one unknown dictionary entry versus one unsupported object while supported content continues. The extension parser accepts arbitrary prefix keys and does not validate public registry membership, consistent with a producer-side name rule, but this is not a test of all unknown-feature handling.

features.requirement: §7.12 defines catalog /Extensions and points to Annex E. §7.7.4 defines the unrelated Name dictionary/name trees (located via catalog /Names).
features.assessment: No §7.7.4 behavior is needed for extension declarations in this assigned scope; do not merge name-tree requirements into the extension registry audit.
